content: RRH peropsin, a receptor resembling visual pigments, is a protein encoded by the RRH gene in humans. Peropsin is classified as an opsin and is therefore part of the guanine nucleotide-binding protein (G protein)-coupled receptor family. The peropsin gene structure includes seven exons, similar to the genes encoding neuropsin and RGR-opsin. Peropsins belong to one of the four subgroups of the Go/RGR opsins, also referred to as RGR/Go or Group 4 opsins. The Go/RGR opsins represent one of the four primary groups of type-II opsins, which are also known as metazoan or animal opsins. The Go/RGR opsins are further divided into four subgroups: Go-opsins, RGR-opsins, peropsins, and neuropsins. Animal opsins are categorized into four major classes: C-opsins (ciliary opsins), R-opsins (rhabdomeric opsins), Cnidops (cnidarian opsins), and Go/RGR-opsins. Among these, three subclades—C-opsins, R-opsins, and Go/RGR-opsins—are found exclusively in Bilateria, while Cnidops are unique to cnidarians. However, the bilaterian clades form a paraphyletic group when Cnidops are excluded.
